visualBrief: Golestan Palace before the March 2026 damage, with the twin towers and clock of Shams-ol Emareh, the blue tiled windcatchers, the Marble Throne terrace, the main halls and the interconnected garden pools.

references.detail: Edifice of the Sun with paired three-storey pavilions, clock, garden iwan and jewel-toned stucco and tile.
Main facade window rhythms, columned entrance and decorative panels.
Tapered turquoise shaft, pale vertical louvres and patterned cornices.
Spiral marble columns, open mirrored terrace, throne platform and supporting figures.
Extent of the palace and composition of the garden and surviving buildings.

limitations: This is a dated reconstruction of the palace and gardens before the damage reported on 2 March 2026. The present-day view retains the current map geometry.

The eight palace complexes are represented by their exterior landmarks. The Marble Throne is visible from the courtyard. Hidden museum interiors, original inscriptions and individual paintings are outside this model.
The Badgir building footprint is inferred from its mapped location, nearby garden setbacks and photos. Facade and roof details interpret the photos.
